citation: Arluke, A., & Luke, C. (1997). Physical cruelty toward animals in Massachusetts, 1975-1996. Society & Animals, 5(3), 195-204.
headline_finding: Only ~0.33% of MSPCA abuse complaints were prosecuted; 70% of prosecuted abusers had prior violent/drug/disorder records.
rigor_note: Massachusetts-specific (state-level, not federal) - assigned to US-FED as the closest available jurisdiction_id since no state-level entries exist in this database. This is the foundational paper that MOTIVATED states to pass felony provisions, not itself a before/after evaluation of felony-provision effects. No later 50-state panel study comparing felony adoption to prosecution/sentencing outcomes was found - a genuine gap.

citation: Palais, J. (2021). Using the National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS) to Study Animal Cruelty: Preliminary Results (2016-2019). Social Sciences, 10(10), 378. DOI 10.3390/socsci10100378.
headline_finding: Descriptive analysis of offender/victim demographics and offense type using 2016-2019 NIBRS data.
rigor_note: Not a causal evaluation of the 2016 NIBRS policy itself - uses NIBRS as a data source to describe patterns, not to evaluate whether adding the category changed enforcement behavior.

outcome_measure: co-occurrence with intimate partner violence, arrest rate
citation: Addington, L., & Randour, M. L. (2024). Using National Incident-Based Reporting System Data to Explore Animal Cruelty Incidents that Occur with Intimate Partner and Family Violence. Journal of Family Violence.
headline_finding: IPV cases co-occurring with animal cruelty had a HIGHER arrest rate than IPV cases co-occurring with other crime types (n=278, 2020 NIBRS data).
rigor_note: Descriptive/bivariate design, not causal. Publisher paywalled on fetch. Direct relevance to 'the Link' and cross-reporting rationale.

citation: Randour, M. L., Kearley, A., & Wireman, C. (2024). Examining Law Enforcement Agencies' Responses to the Addition of Animal Cruelty to NIBRS. American Journal of Criminal Justice, 49(4), 576-589.
headline_finding: Documents uneven agency-level adoption/reporting-compliance patterns following NIBRS category addition.
rigor_note: Studies agency reporting behavior, not crime effects - an important data-quality caveat for anyone using NIBRS as an outcome measure in enforcement_statistics.

citation: Addington, L., & Randour, M. L. (2022). Intentional Cruelty Versus Neglect: New Insights on Animal Cruelty Crimes and Implications for Policy. SAGE. DOI 10.1177/08874034221098918.
headline_finding: New insights on distinguishing intentional cruelty from neglect in cruelty-crime data, with policy implications.
rigor_note: Exact journal title not independently confirmed this round - flagged rather than guessed.

citation: N/A - systematic search found no peer-reviewed study evaluating the Animal Welfare (Sentencing) Act 2021's causal effect on sentence length.
headline_finding: No study found isolating the Act's causal effect on sentencing outcomes.
rigor_note: Two official descriptive-statistics sources exist and are usable for a FUTURE DiD/interrupted-time-series design once enforcement_statistics is populated (Phase 3): Sentencing Council's animal-cruelty statistical bulletin (avg 3,214 prosecutions/year, 63% conviction rate, 2016-2022) and RSPCA Prosecutions Annual Reports (2019: 661 convicted, 93.7% success rate; pre-Act 3-year total: 3,753 convictions, 156 immediate custodial sentences).

outcome_measure: use of new maximum penalties post-2020 Act
citation: Scottish Government (2025). Review of the Animals and Wildlife (Penalties, Protections and Powers) (Scotland) Act 2020.
headline_finding: Courts are NOT using the new maximum penalties; the review concludes not enough time/data exists yet to determine the Act's true sentencing impact, and recommends new sentencing guidelines.
rigor_note: Government self-review (mixed-methods: stakeholder survey + case review), not independent academic research, but methodologically transparent and directly on-point - the closest thing to an official post-implementation evaluation found in the entire literature search.

outcome_measure: average fine amount; average custodial sentence length
citation: Morton, R., Hebart, M. L., & Whittaker, A. L. (2018). Increasing Maximum Penalties for Animal Welfare Offences in South Australia-Has It Caused Penal Change? Animals, 8(12), 236.
headline_finding: Average fines rose from AUD 700 to AUD 1,535 and average prison sentences from 37 to 77 days following South Australia's 2008 penalty-doubling - a real but proportionally modest shift, well below the new statutory maxima.
rigor_note: 314 RSPCA-SA case files, 2006-2018, no control group. THE SINGLE CLEANEST QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN FOUND IN THE ENTIRE LITERATURE SEARCH across all 23 jurisdictions. Study is specific to SOUTH AUSTRALIA (a state not separately represented in this database's jurisdictions table) - assigned to AU-FED as the closest available jurisdiction_id, not a true federal-level finding.

citation: Morton, R., Hebart, M. L., & Whittaker, A. L. (2020). Explaining the Gap Between the Ambitious Goals and Practical Reality of Animal Welfare Law Enforcement: A Review of the Enforcement Gap in Australia. Animals, 10(3), 482.
headline_finding: ~0.5% of cruelty reports nationally result in prosecution; courts impose <10% of available maximum penalties; enforcement heavily outsourced to under-resourced NGOs (RSPCA).
rigor_note: Narrative review across all Australian jurisdictions - closest available 'systematic review of effectiveness' found in the whole literature search.

outcome_measure: charges and sentencing outcomes by offence
citation: Victorian Sentencing Advisory Council (2019). Animal Cruelty Offences in Victoria.
headline_finding: 2,960 charges sentenced across 1,115 cases, 2008-2017, Victorian court records.
rigor_note: Official descriptive report, not a causal evaluation, but a genuine official outcome-data source.

citation: Morton, R., Hebart, M. L., Ankeny, R., & Whittaker, A. L. (2022). Portraying Animal Cruelty: A Thematic Analysis of Australian News Media Reports on Penalties for Animal Cruelty. Animals, 12(21), 2918.
headline_finding: Thematic analysis linking media narrative framing to reform pressure.
rigor_note: Adjacent to policy-effect evidence, not a direct effect study - included for its relevance to understanding reform-pressure dynamics.

citation: Frontiers in Animal Science (2022). Community-expectations survey, n=2,152.
headline_finding: 87.5% of respondents believed cruelty was illegal; 65% wanted the justice system to treat animal-victim cases seriously.
rigor_note: Public-attitudes baseline survey, not a before/after evaluation of any specific reform.

citation: N/A - systematic search found no peer-reviewed empirical evaluation of the 2019 penalty increase (2yr->5yr, JPY2M->JPY5M).
headline_finding: No academic paper regresses arrest trends on the amendment or controls for reporting-awareness confounds.
rigor_note: Raw National Police Agency tracking exists as a genuine descriptive time series (2015=56 arrests -> 2023=181 record high -> 2024=160, already captured in this database's JP-AWMA-P1 provision notes) - available for Phase 3 enforcement_statistics population, but no causal study has been built on it.

citation: Kim, Baek, Ku, & Lee (2026). Companion-Animal Abuse in South Korea: Welfare and Veterinary Implications from Criminal-Court Decisions (2003-2025). Animals, 16(15), 2354.
headline_finding: Content analysis of 501 Supreme Court of Korea judgments (2003-2025): dogs 63.9% of victims; fines-only outcomes in 64.5% of cases vs. imprisonment in 14.1%; veterinary documentation present in only 1.4% of decisions.
rigor_note: Spans the 2017/2021/2022 amendments but does not isolate their effect econometrically - a descriptive content analysis, not a causal design.

outcome_measure: arrest rate, indictment rate, custodial sentencing rate
citation: National Assembly member 강승규 legislative-office data release (2026), citing police/prosecutorial statistics.
headline_finding: 2021-2024 police case volume 4,835 (arrest rate 70.5%); 2020-2024 prosecutorial referrals 4,601 (indictment rate 45.1%); only 29 people received actual prison time nationwide over five years despite statutory-penalty increases - first-instance custodial rate ~7%, fines 68.8%.
rigor_note: Official but not peer-reviewed. Strongest available 'penalties rose on paper, outcomes didn't' data point outside Australia.

citation: HKALPO (Hong Kong Animal Law and Protection Organisation) advocacy data, cited via secondary sources.
headline_finding: Average fines of only ~HK$1,200 in the 18 months following the 2006 amendment (which raised the statutory maximum to HK$200,000); highest-ever sentence since 2006 was 16 months.
rigor_note: Advocacy-organization data, NOT peer-reviewed academic research - but the only available before/after data point suggesting a large gap between statutory maximum and applied sentence.

citation: N/A - systematic search found no empirical evaluation study of the 2015/2017/2022 Taiwan APA amendments.
headline_finding: No empirical evaluation study located.
rigor_note: A 2016 government-sponsored thesis-prize program title suggested relevance but content/authors could not be independently confirmed - flagged unverified, not cited as a real study.

citation: French Senate (2022). Rapport de suivi sur l'application de la loi n. 2021-1539.
headline_finding: The Senate's own oversight report explicitly states that deterrent-effect statistics are NOT YET AVAILABLE - an official acknowledgment that the evaluation has not been done.
rigor_note: A real, citable government oversight document, but it confirms absence of evaluation rather than providing one - hence no_evaluation_found rather than descriptive_only.

outcome_measure: distribution of criminal charge types used as cruelty proxies
citation: Liu, Su, & Nie (2026). Protecting Companion Animals Under Chinese Criminal Law: Current Practice and Future Paths. Animals, 16(14), 2119. DOI 10.3390/ani16142119.
headline_finding: Content analysis of 2,706 first-instance criminal judgments (all 31 provinces, May 2019-May 2026): 16 distinct criminal charges are used to indirectly punish companion-animal harm, confirming no dedicated cruelty offense exists; identifies a total prosecution gap for the abuse-video content industry.
rigor_note: Doctrinal/content analysis, not a before/after evaluation of any specific reform - consistent with CN having no general anti-cruelty offense to evaluate in the first place.

citation: N/A - no compliance or enforcement evaluation found post-enactment of the Shenzhen/Zhuhai 2020 cat/dog-eating bans.
headline_finding: Only 2020 announcement-period news coverage exists; no follow-up evaluation.
rigor_note: Open gap, not further pursued this round.

citation: Advocacy/legal-blog material (unspecified outlets), cited via secondary sources.
headline_finding: Claims that >10% of animals reaching disposal facilities show Animal Protection Act violations, and that enforcement is politically constrained by proximity of local veterinary offices to farms.
rigor_note: NOT confirmed as peer-reviewed - descriptive claims from advocacy/legal-blog sources only.

citation: N/A - Legge 82/2025 took effect 2025-07-01, too recent for any evaluation to exist as of this database's compilation.
headline_finding: Too recent for evaluation - not a gap in search effort.

citation: Tier im Recht (TIR). Swiss Animal Welfare Criminal Practice (annual monitoring report).
headline_finding: Systematic, long-running annual tracking of Swiss animal-welfare criminal practice.
rigor_note: NGO-run, not peer-reviewed, but systematic and long-running - a usable outcome-data source for Phase 3, not itself an evaluation study.
